content:
Hi! I have a formalization of Freek's theorem #50 (The Number of Platonic Solids) that I'd like to
contribute to mathlib.

The proof formalizes the combinatorial characterization: a Schläfli pair (p, q) with p ≥ 3, q ≥ 3 satisfies
1/p + 1/q > 1/2 iff it's one of the five classical pairs. The key inequality 1/p + 1/q > 1/2 is rewritten as
2(p+q) > pq to stay in ℕ. The proof uses upper bounds on p and q (both ≤ 5) via Nat.mul_le_mul, then
interval_cases + omega for exhaustive case analysis.

It builds against Mathlib v4.29.1. Happy to adapt to mathlib conventions — any guidance on:

- Where this should live (Combinatorics? Geometry?)
- Naming conventions for the definitions
- Whether the IsPlatonicPair predicate approach is preferred, or if reviewers would want a different
formulation

Thanks!
Why don't you start by making a downstream repo depending on mathlib and putting it up on GitHub?
Have you used LLMs as part of this project?
Yeah, I used Claude. It was checked by Lean's kernel. I am happy to discuss the workflow if anyone's curious.

This is more or less new policy, but we've decided that the first five PRs from a given contributor should not be AI written: essentially because the review work is typically more than the authorship work at the beginning, and the point of that review work is to help the contributor learn. With an LLM too much in the loop, that learning is an ineffective or unreliable process.
Happy to do my first contributions without LLM assistance. I'll take a look at that file you linked.
Yes, I see it now. Thanks. I can reframe as a corollary

Kim Morrison said:

This is more or less new policy, but we've decided that the first five PRs from a given contributor should not be AI written.

I see this 5 used a lot, so just pointing out that the workflow says PRs <= 5 for new-contributor so you actually have to get 6 PRs in before the label is gone (if LLM ban is based on that).

More on topic, this appears to be the code in Basic? Unless this is some small snippet, this is not really proving what I think you wanted to prove.

You may want to go to the source and look at the HoL version a bit for reference : https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/hol.html#50 ,
Formalizing that 1/p + 1/q > 1/2 has only five solutions with p, q ≥ 3 is trivial, and presumably not what Mathlib wants for a proof.

We have people currently working on convex geometry. There are some vague plans to work on abstract polytopes. These are the things we actually want in a formalization of platonic solids. The inequality on Schläfli symbols should be a corollary, not a defining characteristic.
(the vague plans aren't so vague, but I am not the right person to announce things here)

For mathlib, I think we should arguably also aim for regular polytopes (flag-transitive realizations of abstract polytopes in Euclidean space) that aren't necessarily convex, in any number of dimensions, where the Platonic solids result is just the (convex, 3-dimensional) special case.
We also had #37818 about this, which is similarly strange

Yaël Dillies said:

(the vague plans aren't so vague, but I am not the right person to announce things here)

If there's an active project, I'd like to contribute to it!
